sources.title: City of Lübeck: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries
sources.note: Direct municipal synthesis: restoration, joint appeals court 1820, citizenship reform 1848 and later German statehood. No universal franchise claim.

sources.title: City of Lübeck: Historical chronology
sources.note: Direct city chronology: battle 6 November 1806, occupation to 1813, German Confederation from 1815, railways 1851 and 1865, German Empire 1871.

sources.title: Lübeck Archive: Research on the end of the state in 1937
sources.note: Direct municipal archive announcement of jointly researched book. State ceased 1937 through Greater Hamburg legislation; does not support popular personal-revenge legend.

sources.title: City of Lübeck: Alley and courtyard housing
sources.note: Direct municipal account: medieval origins, stone huts from sixteenth century, rented tiny houses behind merchant street fronts, porters/day laborers/craft workers. Dates not forced to one year.

sources.title: City of Lübeck: The von Höveln alley
sources.note: Indexed original municipal page. Poor/elderly charitable housing established 1483; surviving small houses from comprehensive 1792 rebuilding. Modern ten apartments are 1972 and not projected backward.

sources.title: Lübeck Archive and Hans Meyer: Historic residential building records
sources.note: Direct 18-page PDF, AW.08 Wohnsaal printed page 9 / PDF index 8, Engelswisch 28 Hellgrüner Gang, heading 1797. Exact sample Im Grünen Gang 4 Wohnsäale. Modern compilation transcribes historic Brandassekuranzkasse property record; precise locations uncertain. Page 1 defines individually rented Wohnsaal rooms.

sources.title: Lübeck Foundation Administration: The Holy Spirit Hospital
sources.note: Indexed full original institutional history. Medieval foundation, wooden compartments early nineteenth century, 170 places, last occupants left 1970; rural estate wealth supported building/care.

sources.title: Museum Behnhaus Drägerhaus: The Behnhaus and its domestic rooms
sources.note: Indexed original full text via query site:museum-behnhaus-draegerhaus.de/das-behnhaus Küche. Direct web extraction truncates the interior description. Circa 1800 renovation, Behn family 1823 to 1920, food lift, household plan; green wallpaper is reconstructed from surviving fragment.

sources.title: Hamburg Metropolitan Region: The Wakenitz waterworks in Lübeck
sources.note: Direct official industrial heritage record: operation from 1867, steam pumping of river water, sand filtration and water tower. Avoid applying later 1890 tower alterations to initial plant.

sources.title: Niederegger company archive: History of the confectionery business
sources.note: Direct company historical account used narrowly for its own business dates: 1806 takeover of Maret shop, 1822 move to Breite Straße. Promotional claims about invention/superiority are not used.

sources.title: Museum of the Second World War: The creation of the Free City on 15 November 1920
sources.note: Direct museum historical article. Free City territory, German-speaking majority, League oversight, Polish foreign representation/customs/port rights. Do not copy erroneous reference to Paderewski as serving prime minister in November 1920 or equate constitutional dates.

sources.title: Free City of Danzig: Constitution in its 14 June 1922 publication
sources.note: Direct modern transcription of primary constitution published by A. W. Kafemann in 1922, with original Pomeranian Digital Library links. Article 3 exact German Die Staatsgewalt geht vom Volke aus.; Article 8 male/female citizens over twenty and exclusions; Article 73 equal civic rights. Linked original scans failed in web tool, so public text identifies a transcription and does not claim visual manuscript inspection.

sources.title: Museum of Gdańsk: The Polish Post Office museum and its collections
sources.note: Direct museum account: separate postal services, Polish and German offices, retained equipment/documents/photos; Polish office attacked 1 September 1939. No browser tour opened.

sources.title: City of Gdańsk: The Polish Gymnasium and its former pupils
sources.note: Direct/indexed full municipal historical account using Gedanopedia and 1957 newspaper. First classes 9 May 1922; 199 pupils/10 teachers first year; fees 20 gulden monthly, transfers to commercial schools; some pupils not fluent in Polish. The 1957 reunion rhetoric is not adopted.

sources.title: Museum of Gdańsk: Sport in interwar Gdańsk
sources.note: Direct museum exhibition research: Gedania founded 15 September 1922, about 550 prewar members, men and women, mainly Polish plus Jewish and German members to mid-1930s; 1922 rowing and yacht clubs. Do not move Chychła postwar Olympic gold into Free City years.

sources.title: City of Gdańsk and museum curators: The Szmelter family and its surviving possessions
sources.note: Direct municipal interview with museum historian Piotr Mazurek and historian Bogdan Chrzanowski, family photographs and objects. Gdańsk restaurant tenancy 1933 (not earlier Toruń 1922 to 1932), open all hours, wife Maria accounts and station mission, jobs/housing/overnight assistance. Speculative secret-service funding and escape-route explanations excluded.

sources.title: Museum of Gdańsk and Polish Academy of Sciences Library: Everyday objects of the Free City
sources.note: Direct 2020 museum exhibition announcement with named curator Aneta Kwiatkowska: original library ephemera include non-postage advertising/propaganda labels and confession slips admitting holders to Easter communion. No claim all inhabitants followed this religious practice.

sources.title: German Federal Archives: Danzig under National Socialism
sources.note: Direct national archive account with contemporary photographic records. Nazi majority 28 May 1933, Great Synagogue demolition May 1939, invasion/annexation 1 September 1939, postwar Polish city. Avoid attributing Nazi aggression to Polish defensive measures or repeating archive caption hostile slogans.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum: Danzig and antisemitic persecution
sources.note: Direct museum article and photographs: antisemitic markings on Jewish businesses 1935; forced-closed shop 1939. Overview caption erroneously dates Versailles 1918; use correct 1919 given in main body only if necessary. No harmful slogans quoted.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported 1715 to 1878 record. Decoded 1715 bbox 8.7787,52.6185 to 13.8043,54.3718 is grossly overbroad; later outlines 10.6615,53.6111 to 10.8919,53.8843 fit Lübeck vicinity. Public overview explicitly warns. Research covers city republic, not Prince-Bishopric. Actual state ending 1937 kept separate from map cutoff. No geometry modification proposed.

Decoded 1930 to 1938 Free City of Danzig record: bbox 18.2252,53.9346 to 19.2332,54.4554 fits interwar territory with neighboring communities. Public overview supplies actual 1920 to 1939 interval and distinguishes modern city from regime. Not aliasing medieval Danzig or present Poland. No invented border repair.
